title: Corn, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑sodium canned corn is a ready‑to‑eat product made from mature corn kernels that are cooked, lightly salted, and sealed in airtight cans. No fat is added during processing, making it a convenient low‑salt option for quick meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn has been cultivated for more than 7,000 years and is one of the world’s oldest staple crops.
Canning preserves most B‑vitamins and antioxidants such as lutein.
Reduced‑sodium versions are ideal for people watching their salt intake.
Corn provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.
In the United States canned corn is a common ingredient in salads, chowders, and chili.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements, helps maintain satiety, and supports stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect eye health and reduce oxidative stress in cells.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Reduced salt content is beneficial for blood‑pressure control and cardiovascular risk reduction.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate (B9) aid energy metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Provides magnesium and potassium
items.content: These minerals support muscle function and help maintain electrolyte balance.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to respiratory symptoms.

items.title: Natural sugar content
items.content: Although unsweetened, the natural sugars in corn can affect blood glucose levels in people with diabetes; portion control is advised.

items.title: Can integrity
items.content: If the can is damaged or the product is stored for too long after opening, oxidation may occur; consume within the recommended time.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the corn straight from the can, add it to salads, soups, stews, omelets, or use it as a filling for tacos and burritos. It can also be quickly warmed in a skillet with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and refrigerate for 3–4 days. Discard if you notice off‑odors or discoloration.
